prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a narrow bus aisle bordered by seat backs, with the nearest seats in the lower foreground within roughly 0.3–1 m of the camera wearer and more distant seats receding toward the front. A person moves from approximately 4–5 m away in frame 1 to about 2–3 m in frame 2, around 1.5–2 m in frames 3–4, and roughly 0.7–1 m in frame 5, remaining generally in front of and increasingly to the camera wearer’s right. The brighter foreground surfaces make near/far ordering and the person’s approach clearer than RGB alone, including seat backs that partly occlude the lower body in several frames. Metric distances are only rough because the map has no scale, and large smooth regions—especially the ceiling, windows, person, and similarly shaded seats—contain blurred or inconsistent depth boundaries.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates multiple chairs from the person, showing seats on both sides of the aisle and several overlapping seat backs in the foreground; the nearest chairs are about 0.3–1 m away, while successive rows are roughly 1–4 m away. The person is initially small and partly obscured near the left/front of the aisle, then becomes a larger central-right mask as the separation from the camera wearer falls from roughly 4–5 m to under 1 m; nearby chairs remain between parts of the person and the camera in some frames. It makes object identity and occlusion ordering clearer than RGB, especially where similarly colored seats overlap, but it provides little direct depth information and does not show reliable facing direction beyond the person silhouette. Several chair masks and labels overlap, fragment, or merge with adjacent seats, and parts of the person or chairs near boundaries appear missed or mislabeled.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates one person in frames 3–5, with the skeleton growing larger as the person approaches from roughly 1.5–2 m to about 0.7–1 m in front of the camera wearer; no dependable skeleton is visible in the first two frames despite the person being present in RGB. The torso and head remain broadly oriented toward the camera, while the body shifts from near the center to the right side; in the final frame one arm extends downward and outward, with the hand lying roughly within the person’s own arm’s reach and close to the camera wearer’s near space. The map makes joint arrangement, body orientation, and the final hand location easier to distinguish than RGB, while the black background removes all information about seats, aisle geometry, and body-seat occlusions. Head points are too coarse to establish gaze reliably, several limbs or hands are absent or displaced, and the final magenta hand cluster appears noisy and partly overlaps the lower torso.
